_meta.note: Build the SOURCING BRIDGE (scope-doc phase SB) and the full RESEARCH SKILL (RS) on top of the grounding core (GATE_GR). The actual web FETCH stays on-demand / agent-driven (a CLI can't call WebSearch; the fetch is non-deterministic) — so the CODE deliverables are the two DETERMINISTIC, gate-able bridges: (1) `research-context` — a Seam-2 provider that renders a section's grounded claims (source + excerpt) as the context block fed to the writer (the claim→section bridge into the docs-authoring Seam-2 flow); (2) `stamp-evidence` — computes honest sha256 of the STORED source files and stamps them into evidence.json, so the shas ground-check verifies are trustworthy (computed from what was stored, not agent-supplied). Both node ≡ python. The on-demand fetch (agent uses WebSearch / the deep-research skill → drops raw source text into files → stamp-evidence materializes the map → ground-check gates it → refute) is DOCUMENTED, not a gated CLI. RS extends the research skill to the full loop + a worked example, seeding the refutation with hb-audit --questions. Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted; honest that grounding != truth and the fetch is on-demand.

phases.title: Sourcing bridge — the deterministic research-context + stamp-evidence providers

tasks.title: Spec-first: fixtures + proofs for research-context and stamp-evidence
tasks.description: Author RED-first. Fixtures under plugin/adapters/research/fixtures/: (a) context/evidence.json — an all-grounded evidence map with 2 claims in section 'background' (each with source+url+excerpt) and 1 claim in section 'method' whose excerpt contains the DISTINCTIVE token 'METHOD-ONLY-EXCERPT' (so a section-leak is detectable); (b) unstamped/evidence.json (sources.s1 with NO sha256) + unstamped/sources/s1.txt whose text contains a claim's excerpt, so that after stamping, ground-check reports that claim GROUNDED. Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/research-context.sh (prints RESEARCH-CONTEXT-OK): `node plugin/adapters/research/research-context.js <context/evidence.json> background` renders BOTH background claims (ids + their excerpts + source url) and NOT the method-section claim; node ≡ python byte-identical. Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/stamp-evidence.sh (prints STAMP-EVIDENCE-OK): `node plugin/adapters/research/stamp-evidence.js <unstamped/evidence.json> <unstamped/sources>` outputs an evidence.json whose sources.s1.sha256 = the REAL sha of s1.txt, such that piping it to ground-check yields GROUNDED (was UNGROUNDED-shaless / would-STALE before); node ≡ python produce the SAME stamped map (parsed-equal). Both must FAIL now (no providers yet).

tasks.title: Implement research-context + stamp-evidence (both runtimes)
tasks.description: plugin/adapters/research/research-context.js (export researchContext(evidence, section)) + py twin py/src/heartbeat/adapters/research/research_context.py: for each claim (sorted id) whose section == the given section, render a block — 'Grounded evidence for <section>:' then per claim '  - <id>: <text>' / '    source <sourceId> <url>' / '    » <excerpt>'; '(none)' if no claims. Deterministic; node ≡ python BYTE-identical. plugin/adapters/research/stamp-evidence.js (export stampEvidence(evidence, sourcesDir)) + py twin py/src/heartbeat/adapters/research/stamp_evidence.py: for each source id in evidence.sources, if <sourcesDir>/<id>.txt exists set its sha256 = sha256(file bytes); print the stamped evidence JSON. node ≡ python produce the SAME map. Both import nothing from core, are advisory. CLIs: `research-context.js <evidence.json> <section>`, `stamp-evidence.js <evidence.json> <sourcesDir>`. Add py/tests. Make research-context.sh + stamp-evidence.sh + tests/parity.sh green.

tasks.description: Add groups T112 (research-context.sh → RESEARCH-CONTEXT-OK) and T113 (stamp-evidence.sh → STAMP-EVIDENCE-OK) to tests/run-tests.sh (markers on the same check line).
